There's also a WIP PR against ARIA to account for these changes: https://github.com/w3c/aria/pull/2474

There are some open questions being discussed there on exactly how to refer to the HTML concepts, since ARIA needs to be language-independent, but it will certainly refer to these spec concepts in some form.

> This should be updated to make use of the new [Reflect] syntax.

Thanks @lukewarlow! Fixed now (it wouldn't let me merge the suggestions directly due to merge conflicts).
I'm not sure how GitHub actually lets you dismiss change suggestions but consider this me dropping my change suggestions as they've been resolved :)
My apologies for letting this sit for so long. I've addressed Anne's comments, I think.

Based on discussion in https://github.com/WICG/webcomponents/issues/1114, I wanted to go ahead and fix the reflected attribute values to use a shallower/more naive algorithm. Specifically, we shouldn't need to resolve the reference target _at all_ for reflected attribute getters.

@keithamus suggested it might be good to have separate algorithms for getting the elements referred to by an attribute - one for the "shallow" values, and one for the "resolved" values - which calls into the former.

I thought that was a great idea, so I've now completely renamed what used to be called "(get the) _attr_-associated element(s)" to "(get the) resolved _attr_ target element(s)", with "(get the) unresolved _attr_ target element(s)" as the "shallow" algorithm both the former algorithm and the reflected attribute getter calls into.

It's annoying to rename _attr_-associated elements like this, since it's now a relatively long-standing concept from reflected element attributes and a lot of method names in browsers refer to it directly, _but_ I like the new names because:

- it connects directly with "reference target" - I've also referred to "target" in more places in the prose now, as well
- it means "form-associated element" goes back to having a single meaning (before this change, there was also `form`-associated element, i.e. the element referred to by the `form` attribute - that would now be referred to as the resolved `form` target element).

Alice, Jake, Olli, and I discussed the event model again. Here's the concrete proposal:

- For events that have a non-null source-like concept (such as source or submitter), we set event's relatedTarget concept to that value and we set composed to true at the time we pass the event to the dispatch algorithm. (This is roughly comparable to the current proposal except that intermediate shadow roots are no longer skipped. See https://mozilla.pettay.fi/composed-events-dispatch.html for a visualization.)
- For events with a source-like concept, the IDL getter for that concept now needs to return event's relatedTarget concept.

@annevk I think this basically makes sense. There are a couple details I'm unclear on about setting the event to composed.
- It seems like there is some additional compatibility risk to this. For example, consider the case when the `submit` event is fired on a form due to a button being clicked, with no reference target involved, so the button and form are in the same tree. There would be no change to how the event bubbles, since both `target` (the form) and `relatedTarget` (the button) are in the same tree, but event listeners on the form would still see `event.composed == true`.
  - Maybe we can avoid this by only setting composed if `target` and `relatedTarget` are not in the same tree, which would mean that reference target was being used, which removes the compat concern since it's a new thing?
- When you say "we set composed to true at the time we pass the event to the dispatch algorithm", when exactly does this mean? Usually composed gets set from the HTML spec when it calls [fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire), so maybe we could do it at that time when the HTML spec calls [fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) for Command, Toggle, and Submit events. But it sounds like your idea might have been that we'd set composed inside the DOM spec algos either at the beginning of [dispatch](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch) or right before dispatch, in [fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire)? This might be OK but seems like it could cause compat issues for events like mouseenter that already use `relatedTarget` but are not composed; we’d have to exclude them from the change somehow like by scoping the change to specific event types.

@dandclark thanks, for 1) I think our assessment is that websites are highly unlikely to rely on the `composed` value as we have been able to fiddle with it in the past. For 2) we meant when initializing the specific events under discussion in HTML. Not as a generic solution for all events as that would indeed clash with existing relatedTarget consumers.

Fire an event does run into https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328 which I think @keithamus wanted to look into, but should probably not block this. Maybe we want to add a source comment (`<!-- ... -->`) though.

@annevk Ok, I pushed those changes to this and the DOM spec PR (https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1353).

In these changes I'm trying to draw a distinction between Event's internal [relatedTarget](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-relatedtarget) concept and the `relatedTarget` attribute that gets exposed in other specs like https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-focusevent-relatedtarget. So I changed [fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) to take a separate `relatedTarget` parameter that sets the internal `relatedTarget` concept, rather than reusing the existing machinery that would set it as an attribute. Not sure if that's the right approach to take us in the direction of fixing https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328 or if I should just have all the "fire an event" calls initialize `relatedTarget` as another attribute on the event for now.
I think making _relatedTarget_ a (named) parameter is a good idea.

> @dandclark thanks, for 1) I think our assessment is that websites are highly unlikely to rely on the composed value as we have been able to fiddle with it in the past.

@annevk Do you remember the case(s) when `composed` was fiddled with in the past? That'd be helpful to reference when evaluating possible compat impact here.

> Do you remember the case(s) when composed was fiddled with in the past?

I think we changed it for UI events. And more recently we weren't sure with these toggle events.

----

I fixed quite a few issues with this PR. Further review welcome. The outstanding issue is the synthetic events. It seems we should align them with precedent and have the constructors initialize the relatedTarget concept correctly.
Thanks for taking the time @annevk. I'm going to be out on vacation next week but will make the change for synthetic events when I get back.

One thing I haven't checked in tests: aria-labelledby and non-trivial DOM mutations in multiple levels of nested Shadow DOMs. (Support for aria-labelledby is one thing missing currently in Gecko's referenceTarget implementation)

- I commented [above](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#discussion_r3582673119) about a potential approach for having the constructors set relatedTarget for synthetic events. @annevk if that seems reasonable I'll make those changes.
- @smaug---- there's tests for aria-labelledby at [shadow-dom/reference-target/tentative
/aria-labelledby.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/632a1e7b1b/shadow-dom/reference-target/tentative/aria-labelledby.html), and [shadow-dom/reference-target/tentative
/dom-mutation.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/632a1e7b1be280befa88e7aa3244de5b3fbf37d5/shadow-dom/reference-target/tentative/dom-mutation.html) covers interesting DOM mutation scenarios that include mutations across multiply-nested shadow roots.

@dandclark I had AI perform a check and it still identifies many structural issues with this PR (and it appears to be correct). See https://gist.github.com/annevk/48545a644f86e2536bafc5c437a64517 (starting at line 44 for this PR, the DOM PR is above).

Thanks for flagging [those issues](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#issuecomment-5407025187) @annevk. All the blocking ones are resolved on this and on the [DOM PR](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/1353). Both are ready for another look.
 
A couple of the fixes are worth calling out since they differ from what was decided [here](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995#issuecomment-4572681552). One issue your [AI feedback](https://gist.github.com/annevk/48545a644f86e2536bafc5c437a64517) noticed and that was separately filed as a [Chromium bug](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/559225364) is that for CommandEvent/SubmitEvent if we just naively set the `relatedTarget` to the `source`, then in cases where the `source` is an element in a shadow that targets its own host for the event, the event path will get adjusted to an empty path so that the event won't fire at all. This seems bad.
 
Specifically, in [dispatch](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch) the step *"Let relatedTarget be the result of [retargeting](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#retarget) event’s [relatedTarget](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-relatedtarget) against target.*" initializes relatedTarget as target and then the check *"If target is not relatedTarget or target is event’s [relatedTarget](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-relatedtarget):"* is false so the whole building of the event path is skipped.
 
The way I chose to [fix this in Chromium](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8392862) was that instead of passing the `source`/`submitter` element to dispatch directly as the `relatedTarget`, instead check if the `source`/`submitter` retargeted against `target` equals `target`, and if so, pass `target` as the `relatedTarget` instead of `source`/`submitter`. I updated the HTML spec PR to do this in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995/commits/644c89c3f9b60e3ee91847ceb1698d4f2304173f. I added WPTs for this too: [submit-event-shadow-host.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/47f500f1d7/html/semantics/forms/form-submission-0/submit-event-shadow-host.html), [commandfor-shadow-host.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/47f500f1d7/html/semantics/the-button-element/command-and-commandfor/commandfor-shadow-host.html).
 
The second issue is due to the fact that the event target and relatedTarget are cleared at the end of [dispatch](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch) -- see `clearTargets` in that algorithm. If CommandEvent/SubmitEvent now have their source/submit properties backed by relatedTargets, that means those properties on the Event now get nulled out after dispatch has finished. What I hadn't realized before is that this is a breaking change because it can happen even with no reference target involved -- see https://issues.chromium.org/issues/556160944#comment8.
 
This can be fixed by returning the `source`/`submitter` properties back to being independent from `relatedTarget`; they would once more be backed by the `source`/`submitter` given when the event was created. These events' `relatedTarget` would still be set from `source`/`submitter`, but only for the purpose of affecting event propagation, not for backing these properties. This prevents the breaking change while still avoiding changes to DOM spec event dispatch. I added this change in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10995/commits/9407629c68cb4c4f34c8adfc38653281cabd555a. WPTs were updated accordingly in https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8353650.

@delan should be fixed now.

AI feedback Reviewed at 6d7b2b9. Lint and the remote build pass. The DOM anchors this links to resolve against the rebased whatwg/dom#1353, and most of the earlier AI feedback has been addressed. I rebased this onto main as a single commit (a092f0879) and pushed two commits on top: - 7547a8dbc with editorial fixes: modern algorithm openers and getter steps, possessives for the resolved target elements, `` markup for `Element`, and HTML's convention for named arguments ("relatedTarget set to …"). - 229c48dd6, which needs your review. Main's 985d4435e replaced the prose triggers for resetting form owners with *reset the form owners with a form attribute*, called from DOM hooks. This commit restores this PR's reference target triggers in that model. The algorithm now continues into the host's tree when the host has an ID, and changing a shadow root's reference target runs it as well. The rest of the rebase was mechanical: declarative shadow root parsing had moved for the Sanitizer. I also refreshed web-platform-tests/wpt#51213, which now moves all current reference target tests out of `tentative/`. Coverage for features that aren't standardized (`interestfor`, `anchor`, and cross-root `aria-owns`) stays in `.tentative` files. **Blockers** - The [composed flag](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L65267) is now set unconditionally on `submit`, `toggle`, and `beforetoggle` (six more sites follow the same pattern). When there is no source or submitter, relatedTarget is null, so these events now escape shadow trees. This affects `showPopover()`, `hidePopover()`, light dismiss, `showModal()`, and `requestSubmit()` without a submitter. Chromium only sets composed when there is an invoker, source, or submitter. The earlier AI feedback that called a conditional composed flag a blocker was wrong: with the relatedTarget model, an event whose source is in the same tree still stops at the shadow boundary. Consider a helper that sets relatedTarget and composed only for a non-null source, plus WPTs for the sourceless cases. - A control's form owner can now be a form in a shadow tree, but [`form.elements`](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L49560) is still rooted at the form's root. [`labels`](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L50033) and [constructing the entry list](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L64636) use tree order, which isn't defined across trees. `shadow-dom/reference-target/form.html` expects `elements` to include the outer referencing controls in shadow-including tree order, which is what Chromium does. - [`ElementInternals.form`](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L80771) is still `HTMLFormElement?`, but its getter now returns a retargeted result that can be a shadow host. Elsewhere `form` and `list` were widened to `Element?`, while Chromium uses `HTMLElement?`. A shadow host is always an HTML element, so `HTMLElement?` works for all of them. - In [*get the unresolved attr target elements*](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L5837), "If this has an explicitly set attr-elements" is always true for `FrozenArray`-reflected attributes, because that value starts out as null. So `ariaLabelledByElements` and friends would iterate null and ignore the content attribute. This needs "… that is not null", as in the single-element version. - [Serializing a shadow root](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L153411) appends the reference target without escaping it, so a value containing `"` produces broken or injected markup. Chromium serializes it as a regular attribute. It should be escaped in attribute mode. **Suggestions** - "Must be a valid … attribute" (for example at [`headers`](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L47555) and [`label`'s `for`](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L49862)) isn't defined for the new terms, and [their definitions](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L5666) use a normative "should". Consider defining the authoring requirements directly. - The [resolved and unresolved target algorithms](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L5677) are defined for a reflected target and use its *get the content attribute*. They are also called for `form` and `list`, which have no reflected IDL attribute. The "… exists" checks in the [`ElementInternals` ARIA defaults](https://github.com/dandclark/html/blob/229c48dd6d9801457f674165bd62a6c8725a6f9d/source#L16372) are also no longer well-defined, because the algorithms now exist for any element-reference attribute. Consider passing the element (or `ElementInternals` object) and the attribute name explicitly. - The PR description still refers to get-the-attr-associated-element. It doesn't mention the event changes (composed and relatedTarget for command, toggle, beforetoggle, submit, and focus events) or the IDL type changes. It also doesn't mention that `headers` and `itemref` lookups are now scoped to the element's tree instead of the `Document`, or that `itemref` can now reach into shadow trees. **Nits** - UI Events doesn't define `FocusEvent.relatedTarget` in terms of an event's relatedTarget. HTML now relies on that, because it no longer initializes the attribute. I filed w3c/uievents#425 for it. - The exported `#attr-associated-element` and `#attr-associated-elements` anchors are gone. Consider keeping them as IDs on the unresolved algorithms.
